conclusion.answer: not demonstrated. They are useful as reviewer evidence.
decisive_arc: Gen60: unchanged generator on a repaired corpus - caught every wrong implementation it was allowed to judge, and 4 of 8 banks rejected known-correct code
Gen61: require each test to quote its requirement - no effect; the false accusations already carried genuine verbatim quotes
Gen62: require entailment - removed 158 of 188 tests at precision 0.101, and the screen called that PASSED
Gen63: screen repaired with a retention floor; Gen62 re-scored UNEVALUABLE
Gen64: deletion only with a named extra condition - destruction stopped, retention 0.821 to 0.964, detection restored, and the unsafe rate returned to 4 of 8 on the same four tasks
conclusion.next_branch: a repository-informed checker changes the checker's information boundary and belongs in a new experimental branch, not as another turn of this one
conclusion.question: are model-generated tests safe to use as an unattended gate on this pinned model and generator configuration?
conclusion.scope: one pinned model, one generator contract, one corpus of eight tasks, one run per condition; this is a bounded result, not a general claim about generated tests
conclusion.supported_use: surface suspicious cases for a human reviewer
conclusion.why_filters_failed: the false accusations and the sound inferences are indistinguishable from the information a checker is given - one requirement sentence and one test

contract.no_threshold: this module applies no bar and reaches no verdict; the screen still exists and still runs, and its output is recorded as secondary
contract.reads_only: committed outcome files; no model call, no re-run
contract.replaces: PASSED/FAILED as the headline for the generated-evidence question
reports: wrongs caught out of the eligible population
contract.why: the frozen screen returned PASSED for a run with half its banks unusable, for a run that changed nothing, and for a run that had deleted 84% of its tests; the word tracked none of it
